about.title: Cotati Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Cotati is a small city, but its shops, apartment complexes, and public spaces along corridors like Old Redwood Highway and E Cotati Avenue see steady foot traffic every day. When a property owner lets a spill sit, ignores broken pavement, or ignores poor lighting in a stairwell or parking lot, a routine walk can turn into a serious injury. California law puts the burden on you to show the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why acting quickly matters: photos of the hazard, witness names, and store or building surveillance footage tend to disappear fast. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves — we simply connect people hurt in falls around Cotati with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather evidence before it's lost, and explain your options at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Fast Documentation
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. Photos of the spill, debris, or broken surface taken soon after the fall can make the difference in whether that's provable.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many Cotati businesses record over security footage within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation letter quickly so that video isn't lost before it's ever reviewed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you were partly distracted or moving quickly when you fell, California's pure comparative fault rule means you may still recover a share of damages proportional to the property owner's responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Cotati?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public sidewalk or municipal building in Cotati, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early administrative claim. Talking to an attorney soon after the fall helps make sure you don't miss a critical window.

items.question: What if I fell at a business along Old Redwood Highway or E Cotati Avenue?
items.answer: Falls at retail stores, restaurants, or shopping areas along Cotati's busier corridors often come down to whether staff knew about a spill, torn mat, or uneven walkway and failed to address it in a reasonable time. An attorney can request maintenance logs and incident reports specific to that location to help establish what the owner knew.

items.question: Do I need to prove the property owner was careless on purpose?
items.answer: No, you don't have to show intent. You generally need to show the owner knew about the dangerous condition, or should have discovered it through reasonable inspection, and failed to fix or warn about it. An independent attorney can help sort through what evidence supports that in your specific situation.
